name: Rewind
description: A lightweight, open-source, local-first gaming recorder with instant replay, screen recording, and clip editing. No accounts, no cloud dependency, no telemetry — just capture and save.
readme_summary: Rewind was a lightweight, open-source, local-first gaming recorder designed for instant replay, screen recording, and clip editing. It prioritized performance and privacy by avoiding cloud dependencies, accounts, and telemetry, allowing users to capture and manage their gameplay moments locally. Although development has ceased, the project remains available as a public fork.
key_features: Designed to Stay Out of the Way
primary_use_case: Capturing and editing gameplay moments locally without performance impact or cloud dependency.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan, representing Rewind, is meticulously crafting a perfect, glowing gem (representing a gameplay clip) from a stream of raw, unrefined ore (representing raw gameplay footage). The artisan uses precise tools to shape and polish the gem, discarding excess material. In the background, a small, unobtrusive workbench displays simple UI elements for trimming and adjusting the gem's facets. The scene is bathed in a soft, focused light, emphasizing the creation of a valuable, polished output from raw input. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic, highlighting the local, focused nature of the capture and editing process.

name: contrack
description: Self-hosted contact management + tracking + online enrichment for your personal and professional needs 🐦‍⬛
readme_summary: Contrack is a self-hosted, privacy-focused contact management application designed to consolidate, enrich, and track personal and professional contacts. It aims to give users full ownership of their network by importing contacts from various sources, automatically deduplicating them, enriching profiles with notes and web research, and providing tools to maintain relationships.
key_features: Import contacts from multiple sources (Apple, Google, LinkedIn, Facebook)
Connect calendar/inbox to see past conversations and meetings
Automatic and manual contact deduplication with undo functionality
Enrich contact profiles with notes, dates, tags, and reminders
Web research for automatic profile enrichment with cited sources
Relationship tracking to maintain contact with important people
primary_use_case: To provide individuals with a centralized, self-hosted, and privacy-respecting platform for managing, enriching, and actively tracking their personal and professional contact network.
cover_image_prompt: A meticulous librarian in a grand, organized library, carefully cataloging and cross-referencing ancient scrolls (representing contacts) from various origins. Each scroll is being scanned by a gentle, glowing light that reveals hidden details and connections, transforming them into beautifully bound volumes with rich annotations. Small, subtle digital particles representing data flow around the librarian, and a faint, stylized 'Contrack' logo is etched into a nearby bookshelf. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, emphasizing clarity and order, rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a focus on intricate details and a harmonious color palette.

name: homelable
description: Self-hosted homelab infrastructure visualizer — interactive network diagram with live status monitoring
readme_summary: Homelable is a self-hosted infrastructure visualization tool that scans and monitors your homelab network. It generates interactive network diagrams, provides live status updates, and integrates device documentation directly into the visualization.
primary_use_case: Visualizing and monitoring self-hosted homelab infrastructure.
cover_image_prompt: A meticulous cartographer in a cozy, dimly lit study, using a magical quill to draw an intricate, glowing map of a bustling digital city. The map dynamically updates with live data streams, showing connected devices as vibrant buildings and active services as pulsing lights. Small, transparent screens float around the cartographer, displaying network topology, device health statuses, and snippets of code. The repository name 'Homelable' is subtly etched onto the cartographer's desk. The scene is rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style, with a warm, inviting color palette and a focus on clear, readable details.

name: proxmox-manager
description: Proxmox VM/CT Management Tool – A robust Bash TUI for managing Proxmox virtual machines and containers. Features include listing, status, start/stop/restart, snapshot management, console access, SPICE integration, and permission checks.
readme_summary: Proxmox Manager is a single-file Bash script that provides a Text-based User Interface (TUI) for managing Proxmox Virtual Machines (VMs) and Containers (CTs). It offers essential management functions without external dependencies, focusing on ease of use and direct interaction with Proxmox VE.
key_features: Alerting via ntfy/email for status changes
primary_use_case: To provide a convenient and efficient command-line interface for managing Proxmox VE virtual machines and containers, especially for users who prefer TUI environments or need a lightweight, dependency-free solution.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled technician, depicted as a friendly robot, is orchestrating a miniature cityscape of interconnected servers and virtual machines. The robot is using a holographic console, displaying live data streams and simple icons representing running VMs and containers. One hand is gesturing towards a 'start' button, causing a small virtual machine to glow and power up, while the other is managing a 'snapshot' icon that creates a shimmering duplicate. Subtle digital particles flow from the console to the virtual machines, indicating control and management. The overall mood is efficient and organized, with a clean, modern aesthetic. The 'Proxmox Manager' name is subtly integrated into the holographic display. Style: 3D isometric illustration with clear, vibrant colors and soft lighting.

name: wavemon
description: wavemon is an ncurses-based monitoring application for wireless network devices on Linux.
readme_summary: wavemon is a C-based, ncurses-enabled monitoring application for Linux that provides real-time insights into wireless network devices. It displays signal and noise levels, packet statistics, device configuration, and network parameters, working with most Linux kernel-supported wireless hardware.
key_features: Real-time monitoring of wireless network devices
Provides device configuration and network parameters
Supports devices compatible with the Linux kernel
primary_use_case: Monitoring the status and performance of wireless network interfaces on Linux systems through a text-based user interface.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic signal wave character holding a magnifying glass, intently examining a stylized Wi-Fi router. The wave character is surrounded by glowing data streams representing signal strength, packet flow, and network configuration details. Small, subtle UI elements resembling a terminal window with graphs and statistics are embedded in the background. The scene is set in a clean, modern digital space with a soft blue and green color palette, emphasizing clarity and information. The overall style should be a 3D isometric illustration, making the data and the character easily understandable as a representation of monitoring wireless network activity.

name: ghgrab
description: A simple, pretty terminal tool that lets you browse and download files from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, and Forgejo without leaving your CLI.
readme_summary: ghgrab is a command-line interface tool built with Rust that allows users to browse and download specific files or folders from various Git forges like GitHub, GitLab, and others directly from their terminal. It features a user-friendly TUI for easy navigation, file preview, and efficient selection, avoiding the need for full repository clones.
key_features: Browse and download files/folders from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, Forgejo
Terminal User Interface (TUI) for easy navigation and selection
Fuzzy search for quick file and repository discovery
Support for GitHub LFS (Large File Storage)
Batch download of multiple files and folders
Download GitHub release artifacts with OS/architecture awareness
Quick repository search from home screen (GitHub only)
Multiple installation methods (NPM, Cargo, pipx, Nix, AUR)
primary_use_case: To efficiently browse and download specific files or folders from remote Git repositories without performing a full clone, directly from the command line.
cover_image_prompt: A digital librarian meticulously selecting individual books from a vast, glowing library of code repositories, each represented as a distinct shelf. The librarian uses a futuristic tablet displaying a file tree and preview pane to pinpoint exact files or folders. Instead of taking entire shelves (full clones), they are carefully extracting only the desired volumes and placing them into a personalized satchel. Subtle UI elements and data streams flow around the librarian, indicating the 'ghgrab' tool's seamless operation. The scene is set in a clean, modern digital space with a focus on precision and efficiency, rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a vibrant, tech-inspired color palette.
